definitions.doc_after:
Specify controlled WDM populations spanning particle mass, epoch, profile response and
host scatter.

Returns
-------
dict
    Case names mapped to (particle mass in keV, explicit population settings).

Notes
-----
The retained default scatter sigma(log10(c)) = 0.128 dex is the Ishiyama et al. Eq. (7),
Fig. 10 value for z=0 halos of 1e9 to 1e10 solar masses; Hiroshima et al. adopt the
rounded value 0.13 dex. Using one value across masses and redshifts is a model
assumption, not a quadrature error or a new calibration.

This comparison is pinned to the script-declared reference and ITAMAE revisions. Each
source is imported in a fresh process. The output records failures as well as finite
population/rate differences; reference agreement is historical/numerical evidence, not a
calibration of the EPS approximation.

References
----------

.. [cite-scatter] Ishiyama et al. (2013), The Cosmogrid Simulation: Statistical Properties of Small Dark Matter Halos, Eq. (7), Fig. 10.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.2020

.. [cite-structure] Hiroshima, Ando & Ishiyama (2018), Modeling evolution of dark matter substructure and annihilation boost, Section II, Eqs. (4)-(9), (28), (34).
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.07691

Evaluate the WDM virial host mass with the prescribed deterministic offset when
selected.

Parameters
----------
z : float or array_like
    Dimensionless redshift. The cosmological background requires z > -1; population
    nodes use nonnegative redshifts.

Returns
-------
array_like
    Virial host mass in physical Msun, including the explicit N_hermNa=1 scatter rule.

Notes
-----
The median host history follows Correa et al.; the 0.12/0.15 log-mass scatter follows
Yang et al., Eq. (21). The deterministic low-redshift scatter is anchored at z=1 by the
retained upstream implementation; that extension is not quoted as a separate paper
calibration.

Population stages use physical Msun, Mpc and Msun/Mpc^3. Local structure calls
explicitly convert to CGS; no time or h conversion is implicit in the shared solver.
Redshift decreases from accretion to observation, so the positive dm/dz law removes
mass.

References
----------

.. [cite-yang] Yang et al. (2011), An Analytical Model for the Accretion of Dark Matter Subhalos, Eqs. (7)-(16), (21).
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.1757

definitions.doc_after:
Thermal WDM with the Viel transfer amplitude squared and a fixed specification.

Canonical catalogs use Msun, Mpc and Msun/Mpc^3. Tuple conversion uses the
historical Msun, kpc and Msun/pc^3 format. No legacy calculation is provided.

Parameters
----------
mass_wdm : float
    Positive thermal-relic WDM particle mass, numerical value in keV.
wdm_power_convention : str, optional
    Supported standard-t2-q10 convention: the Viel transfer amplitude is squared in
    power. Historical published-q5 selectors are rejected.
cosmology_backend : CosmologyBackend, optional
    ITAMAE background provider. The variant checks compatibility with the cosmology of
    its fitted halo relations.
unit_backend : UnitBackend, optional
    Explicit converter to canonical Msun, Mpc and Msun/Mpc^3 catalogue arrays;
    NativeUnits is the default.

Notes
-----
Viel et al. give the thermal-relic amplitude T = [1+(alpha*k)**(2*nu)]**(-5/nu),
nu=1.12, and alpha=0.049*(m/keV)**(-1.11)*(Omega_WDM/0.25)**0.11*(h/0.7)**1.22 in Mpc/h.
Power uses T**2, hence exponent -10/nu; k is in h/Mpc.

The supported power ratio is T(k)**2=[1+(alpha*k)**(2*nu)]**(-10/nu), with nu=1.12.
Canonical catalogues use Msun, Mpc and Msun/Mpc^3; the compatibility tuple uses Msun,
kpc and Msun/pc^3. No historical q5 calculation is silently converted to this
specification.

References
----------

.. [cite-viel] Viel et al. (2005), Constraining warm dark matter candidates including sterile neutrinos and light gravitinos with WMAP and the Lyman-alpha forest, Eqs. (6)-(7).
    https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0501562

definitions.doc_after:
Calculate one named physical WDM catalog with explicit numerical inputs.

Parameters
----------
M0 : float
    Positive z=0 host M200 in physical Msun.
redshift : float or array_like
    Dimensionless redshift. The cosmological background requires z > -1; population
    nodes use nonnegative redshifts.
dz : float
    Positive nominal spacing of the accretion-redshift quadrature grid.
zmax : float
    Largest requested accretion redshift, above the target epoch; the actual grid
    convention belongs to this variant.
N_ma : int
    Number of logarithmically spaced accretion-mass nodes.
sigmalogc : float
    Nonnegative standard deviation of log10 concentration, in dex.
N_herm : int
    Positive Gauss-Hermite quadrature order for the scatter integrated by this routine:
    concentration in catalogue stages or host history in Na_calc.
logmamin : float, optional
    Lower or upper log10(M200_acc/Msun) bound. A None upper bound uses the model
    host-relative mass limit.
logmamax : float, optional
    Lower or upper log10(M200_acc/Msun) bound. A None upper bound uses the model
    host-relative mass limit.
sigmafac : float
    Deterministic host-history offset in units of log-mass scatter when N_hermNa=1;
    low-redshift scatter is anchored at exactly z=1.
N_hermNa : int
    Positive Gauss-Hermite order for the host-history scatter in the EPS accretion rate.
profile_change : bool
    Apply the variant tidal response of scale radius and density in addition to
    bound-mass loss.
method : str
    picard_table (default), dop853 or odeint for population evolution; the Picard
    adapter itself accepts only the first two.
**solver_options : dict
    Explicit numerical keyword controls for the selected tidal method; stored in
    calculation provenance.

Returns
-------
WeightedSubhaloCatalog
    Canonical physical columns with separate population, concentration and strict
    c_t>0.77 survival weights.

Notes
-----
The retained default scatter sigma(log10(c)) = 0.128 dex is the Ishiyama et al. Eq. (7),
Fig. 10 value for z=0 halos of 1e9 to 1e10 solar masses; Hiroshima et al. adopt the
rounded value 0.13 dex. Using one value across masses and redshifts is a model
assumption, not a quadrature error or a new calibration. The literature threshold rt/rs
> 0.77 follows the Hayashi et al. disruption prescription adopted by Hiroshima et al. A
caller-supplied threshold takes precedence in variants that expose it (C and SI
currently default to 0). This is a model selection rule; an exact-boundary test does not
calibrate disruption physics.

Host M0 is physical M200 at z=0. All accretion nodes are retained and weight_final
applies the strict survival mask. The retained arange(target+dz,zmax+dz,dz) convention
can exceed a non-aligned zmax by less than one nominal step. A wholly zero-measure WDM
population remains zero rather than being renormalized to NaN.

References
----------

.. [cite-scatter] Ishiyama et al. (2013), The Cosmogrid Simulation: Statistical Properties of Small Dark Matter Halos, Eq. (7), Fig. 10.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.2020

.. [cite-structure] Hiroshima, Ando & Ishiyama (2018), Modeling evolution of dark matter substructure and annihilation boost, Section II, Eqs. (4)-(9), (28), (34).
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.07691

.. [cite-survival] Hayashi et al. (2003), The Structural Evolution of Substructure, Section 2.1.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0203004

definitions.doc_after:
Prepare the WDM history coefficients for a fixed host and anchor.

Parameters
----------
M0 : float
    Positive z=0 host M200 in physical Msun.
zi : float or array_like
    Dimensionless redshift. The cosmological background requires z > -1; population
    nodes use nonnegative redshifts.

Returns
-------
tuple
    Reference-epoch M200, alpha and beta of M(z)=M(zi)*(1+z-zi)**alpha*exp[beta*(z-zi)].

Notes
-----
The mass-history coefficients, including q = 4.137 / zf**0.9476 and the polynomial for
zf, follow Correa et al., Section 3. Their original calibration is retained while the
configured background is used; changing the background does not recalibrate the fit.

The public WDM model uses the bundled WMAP7 spectrum and q10 thermal suppression.
Retained structure kernels use CGS mass/radius/density, while host histories and EPS use
numerical physical Msun. Each boundary is explicit; the fixed-gap EPS normalization
remains an approximation even though the WDM collapse barrier depends on mass.

The variance in this history is integrated from the configured WDM spectrum. The
Ludlow Appendix C analytic CDM variance fit is not used by this routine; the
coefficient 1.686 is already present in Correa et al. Eq. (7).

References
----------

.. [cite-correa] Correa et al. (2015), The accretion history of dark matter haloes - III. A physical model for the concentration-mass relation, Section 3 and Appendix B.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.00391

Retained structure kernels use CGS mass/radius/density, while host histories and EPS use
numerical physical Msun. Each boundary is explicit; the fixed-gap EPS normalization

definitions.doc_after:
Return the retained Yang EPS approximation on its active support.

The analytic normalization treats the barrier gap as fixed. Retaining
the mass-dependent WDM collapse threshold does not make this an exact
moving-barrier first-crossing solution.

Parameters
----------
ma : float or array_like
    Positive subhalo mass at accretion, in the same units as reference_mass; endpoint
    queries broadcast over mass and redshift.
zacc : numpy.ndarray
    One-dimensional dimensionless accretion-redshift grid, paired with the population
    grid first axis.
Mhost : float
    Reference host M200 in the variant internal mass unit. M0 normally refers to z=0;
    explicit epoch flags are described by the caller.
z0 : float
    Target or reference redshift specified by the routine; the tidal ODE evolves from za
    down to this epoch.
N_herm : int
    Positive Gauss-Hermite quadrature order for the scatter integrated by this routine:
    concentration in catalogue stages or host history in Na_calc.
Nrand : int
    Number of points in the deterministic auxiliary redshift inversion grid; despite its
    name, this is not a Monte Carlo sample size.
sigmafac : float
    Deterministic host-history offset in units of log-mass scatter when N_hermNa=1;
    low-redshift scatter is anchored at exactly z=1.

Returns
-------
numpy.ndarray
    Expected accretion count per d ln(ma) d ln(1+zacc), with the accretion-redshift axis
    first.

Notes
-----
The EPS accretion kernel and, where used, host-history scatter 0.12-0.15*log10(Ma/M0)
follow Yang et al., Eqs. (12)-(14), (21). Finite-gap normalization and zero-barrier
limits are numerical treatments of that kernel, not new empirical fits.

Only ma<mmax enters the EPS kernel. Variance gaps are integrated directly over the
sharp-k interval to preserve small positive support near saturation. For N_herm=1 the
deterministic scatter law is anchored at exactly z=1; otherwise Gauss-Hermite averages
the host-history distribution.

References
----------

.. [cite-yang] Yang et al. (2011), An Analytical Model for the Accretion of Dark Matter Subhalos, Eqs. (7)-(16), (21).
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.1757

definitions.doc_after:
Return dN/dm of current survivors using bound or accretion mass.

Both displays apply tidal evolution and survival at the observation
redshift. accretion=True changes the mass coordinate to ma200 only.
Returned m is the logarithmic bin center in Msun.

Parameters
----------
M0 : float
    Positive z=0 host M200 in physical Msun.
accretion : bool
    Display accretion rather than present bound mass while retaining survival at the
    observation epoch.
redshift : float or array_like
    Dimensionless redshift. The cosmological background requires z > -1; population
    nodes use nonnegative redshifts.
dz : float
    Positive nominal spacing of the accretion-redshift quadrature grid.
zmax : float
    Largest requested accretion redshift, above the target epoch; the actual grid
    convention belongs to this variant.
N_ma : int
    Number of logarithmically spaced accretion-mass nodes.
sigmalogc : float
    Nonnegative standard deviation of log10 concentration, in dex.
N_herm : int
    Positive Gauss-Hermite quadrature order for the scatter integrated by this routine:
    concentration in catalogue stages or host history in Na_calc.
logmamin : float, optional
    Lower or upper log10(M200_acc/Msun) bound. A None upper bound uses the model
    host-relative mass limit.
logmamax : float, optional
    Lower or upper log10(M200_acc/Msun) bound. A None upper bound uses the model
    host-relative mass limit.
sigmafac : float
    Deterministic host-history offset in units of log-mass scatter when N_hermNa=1;
    low-redshift scatter is anchored at exactly z=1.
N_hermNa : int
    Positive Gauss-Hermite order for the host-history scatter in the EPS accretion rate.
profile_change : bool
    Apply the variant tidal response of scale radius and density in addition to
    bound-mass loss.

Returns
-------
tuple of numpy.ndarray
    Mass-bin centers in Msun and dN/dm in inverse Msun for surviving nodes.

Notes
-----
The retained default scatter sigma(log10(c)) = 0.128 dex is the Ishiyama et al. Eq. (7),
Fig. 10 value for z=0 halos of 1e9 to 1e10 solar masses; Hiroshima et al. adopt the
rounded value 0.13 dex. Using one value across masses and redshifts is a model
assumption, not a quadrature error or a new calibration. The literature threshold rt/rs
> 0.77 follows the Hayashi et al. disruption prescription adopted by Hiroshima et al. A
caller-supplied threshold takes precedence in variants that expose it (C and SI
currently default to 0). This is a model selection rule; an exact-boundary test does not
calibrate disruption physics.

The public WDM model uses the bundled WMAP7 spectrum and q10 thermal suppression.
Retained structure kernels use CGS mass/radius/density, while host histories and EPS use
numerical physical Msun. Each boundary is explicit; the fixed-gap EPS normalization
remains an approximation even though the WDM collapse barrier depends on mass.

References
----------

.. [cite-scatter] Ishiyama et al. (2013), The Cosmogrid Simulation: Statistical Properties of Small Dark Matter Halos, Eq. (7), Fig. 10.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.2020

.. [cite-structure] Hiroshima, Ando & Ishiyama (2018), Modeling evolution of dark matter substructure and annihilation boost, Section II, Eqs. (4)-(9), (28), (34).
    https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.07691

.. [cite-survival] Hayashi et al. (2003), The Structural Evolution of Substructure, Section 2.1.
    https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0203004

    Finite nonnegative CDM table power in (Mpc/h)**3, interpolated
    linearly in k between the supplied knots.
alpha : float
    Nonnegative Viel suppression length in Mpc/h; alpha=0 is CDM.
sigma8 : float
    Positive target rms density contrast at redshift zero.
radius : float, optional
    Top-hat radius in Mpc/h. The WDM model uses 8, independently of the
    sharp-k halo mass assignment.
order : int, optional
    Gauss-Legendre nodes in log(k) in each original table interval.
    Increase this to check quadrature convergence, not to change sigma8.

Returns
-------
float
    N=sqrt(integral[dln(k) k**3 P_CDM(k) T(k)**2 W(k R)**2 /
    (2*pi**2)])/sigma8. Both EPS and concentration use P_WDM/N**2.

Raises
------
ValueError
    If the table, physical inputs, quadrature order or integrated power
    are invalid. No power outside the supplied table is invented.

Notes
-----
Viel et al. give the thermal-relic amplitude T = [1+(alpha*k)**(2*nu)]**(-5/nu),
nu=1.12, and alpha=0.049*(m/keV)**(-1.11)*(Omega_WDM/0.25)**0.11*(h/0.7)**1.22 in Mpc/h.
Power uses T**2, hence exponent -10/nu; k is in h/Mpc.

T(k)**2=[1+(alpha*k)**(2*1.12)]**(-10/1.12). The radius belongs to
the conventional sigma8 definition, not to M=(4*pi/3)*rho*(2.5 R)**3.
The finite table and fixed quadrature have numerical limits; agreement
with an independent integral does not calibrate the halo model.

wmap.title: Komatsu et al. (2011), Seven-Year Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe Observations: Cosmological Interpretation.
wmap.manual_comparison: The paper is real and reachable, but the input header (Omega_b=0.0469, Omega_m=0.27, h=0.7, n_s=0.95, sigma8=0.82) is not a literal Table 1 column. In particular 0.0469 and 0.95 are absent as the cited best-fit values. The WMAP7 label is contextual; exact table-generation parameters are not established by this citation.

growth.title: Carroll, Press & Turner (1992), The Cosmological Constant, Section 3.5.
growth.manual_comparison: The displayed growth suppression is g=2.5*Omega_m/[Omega_m^(4/7)-Omega_Lambda+(1+Omega_m/2)*(1+Omega_Lambda/70)]. The normalized D(z)=g(z)/[(1+z)*g(0)] and code redshift derivatives are derived uses. The DOI reaches a publisher landing page; the NED equation image provides accessible full text.

ludlow.title: Ludlow et al. (2016), The mass-concentration-redshift relation of cold and warm dark matter haloes, Appendix C.
ludlow.location: Eq. (3) and following text, p.5; Appendix C, pp.18-19, Eqs. (C8)-(C12)
ludlow.manual_comparison: The paper explicitly uses delta_sc(z)=1.686/D(z). The variance fit is sigma=22.26*xi^0.292/(1+1.53*xi^0.275+3.36*xi^0.198), xi=(M/(1e10 h^-1 Msun))^-1. It reports about 2.5% fit accuracy over 1e-7 to 1e15 h^-1 Msun. Differentiation is derived. WDM host histories integrate their spectrum and do not use this CDM variance fit; their redundant citation was removed.

formation.title: Ludlow et al. (2016), The mass-concentration-redshift relation of cold and warm dark matter haloes, Section 4.3, Eqs. (6)-(7).
formation.location: Section 4.3, Eqs. (6)-(7), p.11; parameter choices pp.12-13
formation.manual_comparison: The density/formation-time relation and erfc collapsed-mass equation are printed, with f=0.02 and C=650. The published analytic model adopts an Einasto profile with alpha=0.18. Using the NFW mass fraction and a rounded cube-root exponent in the retained solver is an adaptation, not a literal reproduction of that profile model.

correa.title: Correa et al. (2015), The accretion history of dark matter haloes - III. A physical model for the concentration-mass relation, Section 3 and Appendix B.
correa.location: Section 3, Eqs. (2)-(8), p.4; Appendix B, Eq. (B1), p.17
correa.manual_comparison: The anchored mass history, q=4.137*z_f^-0.9476 and z_f=-0.0064*log10(M)^2+0.0237*log10(M)+1.8837 are printed. Appendix B supplies both concentration-redshift branches and their coefficients. M is in physical Msun in these fits. History differentiation and combining a WDM spectrum with these coefficients are derived/adopted uses, not a WDM recalibration.

virial.title: Bryan & Norman (1998), Statistical Properties of X-ray Clusters: Analytic and Numerical Comparisons, Eq. (6).
virial.manual_comparison: For a flat matter-plus-Lambda cosmology the critical-density overdensity is 18*pi^2+82*x-39*x^2, x=Omega_m(z)-1. The paper reports roughly 1% fit accuracy for Omega_m(z)=0.1 to 1. This is distinct from a numerical solver tolerance and from an overdensity relative to mean matter.

conversion.title: Hu & Kravtsov (2003), Sample Variance Considerations for Cluster Surveys, Appendix C.
conversion.manual_comparison: The NFW mass-conversion approximation and inverse-fit coefficients are present. Eq. (C11) has a1=0.5116, a2=-0.4283, a3=-0.00313, a4=-3.52e-5, matching the code. The first value is 0.5116, not 1.5116. Root solving against the exact enclosed-mass identity is a separate derived conversion path.

nfw.title: Navarro, Frenk & White (1997), A Universal Density Profile from Hierarchical Clustering.
nfw.manual_comparison: The density and circular-speed laws are printed. f(x)=ln(1+x)-x/(1+x) follows by integrating the density. Potential with zero at infinity, exact mass-conversion root finding, and c=-1/W0(-exp[-(y+1)])-1 are derived consequences; the paper does not print the implementation's inverse or solver. The 2.163 and 4.625 factors are rounded maximum-speed identities.

structure.title: Hiroshima, Ando & Ishiyama (2018), Modeling evolution of dark matter substructure and annihilation boost, Section II, Eqs. (5)-(9).
structure.manual_comparison: The paper gives the concentration prescription, NFW speed/radius conversion and tidal structural response. Section II adopts scatter 0.13 dex; the disruption discussion and later selection factors use r_t/r_s=0.77. C/SI defaults allowing zero cutoff and all public 0.128-dex scatter defaults are explicit implementation choices, not literal copies of every population setting.

time.title: Jiang & van den Bosch (2016), Statistics of Dark Matter Substructure: I. Model and Universal Fitting Functions, Eq. (2).
time.manual_comparison: tau_dyn=1.628 h^-1 Gyr*(Delta_vir/178)^(-1/2)*(H/H0)^(-1) is explicitly printed. Conversions to the internal time unit and the sign of the redshift derivative are implementation consequences of this positive timescale.

yang.title: Yang et al. (2011), An Analytical Model for the Accretion of Dark Matter Subhalos, Eqs. (12)-(14), (21).
yang.manual_comparison: The unnormalized EPS kernels, support normalization and sigma_log10(Ma)=0.12-0.15*log10(Ma/M0) are printed. Incomplete-gamma normalization and the continuous zero-gap limit are derived evaluations of Eqs. (8)-(9) and (12)-(14). WDM mass-dependent barriers and a fixed-gap normalization are a declared approximation; the low-redshift quantile continuation is not a new printed Yang equation.

tracks.title: Penarrubia et al. (2010), The impact of dark matter cusps and cores on the satellite galaxy population around spiral galaxies, Eq. (8), Fig. 6.
tracks.location: Eq. (8) and Fig. 6, p.8, gamma=1 row
tracks.manual_comparison: The response g(x)=2^mu*x^eta/(1+x)^mu has (mu,eta)=(0.4,0.3) for Vmax and (-0.3,0.4) for rmax in the gamma=1 row. Both displayed rows match the implementation. Applying this CDM tidal response before the SIDM correction or to a suppressed-power population is model composition.

survival.title: Hayashi et al. (2003), The Structural Evolution of Substructure.
survival.manual_comparison: The approximately 0.77*r_s bound concerns instantaneously truncated isotropic NFW systems. Adopting it as a subhalo survival selection follows the later Hiroshima prescription; it is not a universal empirical disruption threshold. Tests at the exact boundary establish mask and inversion behavior only.

scatter.title: Ishiyama et al. (2013), The Cosmogrid Simulation: Statistical Properties of Small Dark Matter Halos, Eq. (7), Fig. 10.
scatter.location: Eq. (7), Fig. 10 and accompanying text, p.10
scatter.manual_comparison: The reported width is 0.128 dex for c_vmax at z=0 and masses 1e9 to 1e10 Msun; the two other bins give 0.124 and 0.125. For an NFW profile c=2.163*c_vmax preserves logarithmic width. All directly exposed defaults inspected here are 0.128, consistent with their existing docs; Hiroshima rounds to 0.13. Extending a constant width across mass/redshift is an assumption.

viel.title: Viel et al. (2005), Constraining warm dark matter candidates including sterile neutrinos and light gravitinos with WMAP and the Lyman-alpha forest, Eqs. (6)-(7).
viel.manual_comparison: The amplitude T=[1+(alpha*k)^(2*nu)]^(-5/nu), nu=1.12 and alpha=0.049*(m/keV)^-1.11*(Omega_WDM/0.25)^0.11*(h/0.7)^1.22 h^-1 Mpc are printed. The power ratio has exponent -10/nu by squaring. The paper states k<5 h/Mpc for this fit. A q5 power control is historical and does not reproduce the squared transfer law.

sharp.title: Schneider (2015), Structure formation with suppressed small-scale perturbations, Eqs. (10)-(12).
sharp.manual_comparison: The sharp-k filter and M=(4*pi/3)*rho*(c*R)^3 mapping with c=2.5 are present. This calibrated mass mapping does not change the real-space top-hat definition of sigma8. The DOI returned HTTP 403 in this audit; the matching arXiv abstract and v2 PDF returned 200.

benson.title: Benson et al. (2013), Dark Matter Halo Merger Histories Beyond Cold Dark Matter: I - Methods and Application to Warm Dark Matter, Eqs. (7)-(10).
benson.manual_comparison: The barrier, Jeans-mass scaling and coefficients 0.04, 2.3, 0.31687, 0.809, 3.06e8, g_X=1.5, 3600, 2.4 and 0.1 are printed. The paper writes log(M/M_J) without specifying a base in this passage. The retained np.log uses the natural logarithm. Coefficient existence is verified; equality of this log convention is not established by the cited text.

wtidal.title: Dekker et al. (2022), Warm dark matter constraints using Milky-Way satellite observations and subhalo evolution modeling, Appendix C.
wtidal.manual_comparison: The functional fits are present, but the printed A coefficients are [-0.0019,0.045,0.0097,-0.31] and zeta coefficients [-0.000056,0.0014,0.00033,-0.0081]. Code keeps -0.313 and [-0.0000555,0.00143,0.000334,-0.00811] from author upstream 99dfc3632eec0126080c0273ddf78f84fe09216c. Those extra digits have implementation provenance, not literal paper support or demonstrated extra accuracy.

constants.title: Mohr & Taylor (2005), CODATA recommended values of the fundamental physical constants: 2002, Table XXVI.
constants.manual_comparison: CODATA 2002 gives G=6.6742(10)e-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2, equivalent to the retained 6.6742e-8 cgs value. It is a historical adopted constant. Rounded parsec, solar-mass and time conversion constants are not newly attributed to this table.
